 These Appeals, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1.

In respect of an accident, which is not in dispute that the Tribunal has awarded the following sums :
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)

1. For Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 32,952/-
 3. Attendant charges 8,000/-
Conveyance, diet, extra nourishment 4. 10,000/-
charges food and attendant charges 5. Loss of income during laid up period 10,000/-
6. Loss of future earning capacity on account of permanent physical 97,200/- disability 7. Loss of amenities and enjoyment of 10,000/-
 life  Total 2,08,152/-
2.
The Tribunal has noticed that the offending vehicle in which the claimant was travelling was covered only with a liability policy.
But, yet it has proceeded to fasten statutory the liability on the insurer.

In view of the fact that the offending vehicle was covered only with a statutory liability policy, the insurer would not be liable to pay the compensation in respect of the injury suffered by the pillion rider.
Therefore, fastening of liability on the insurer is set aside and it is held that the owner of the offending vehicle alone would be liable for the accident.
3. In my view, the sums awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and do not call for any enhancement.
Consequently, the appeal filed by the claimant is dismissed.
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is disposed off.
